definition: A push or a pull on an object, measured in newtons (N); it has a direction as well as a size, and it can change an object's size, shape, speed or direction of motion.
The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting on an object together; when it is zero, the object stays at rest or moves at a constant speed in a straight line.
Describes an object that goes back to its original size and shape when the force on it is removed.
A graph of the load on a stretched object, such as a spring, against its extension; while the extension is directly proportional to the load, it is a straight line through the origin.
The force per unit extension of a spring, $k = \frac{F}{x}$, in N/m or N/cm; it is constant only up to the limit of proportionality, and a stiffer spring has a larger $k$.
The point on a load-extension graph beyond which the extension is no longer directly proportional to the load; the straight line through the origin ends there.
An object stays at rest, or keeps moving at a constant speed in a straight line, unless a resultant force acts on it.
A force between two surfaces that touch, which can oppose their motion over each other and heats them when they rub.
Friction on an object moving through a liquid or a gas, such as air resistance; it acts against the motion and gets bigger as the speed increases.
Motion along a circular path; at a constant speed it needs a resultant force perpendicular to the motion, towards the centre, which changes the direction of the velocity but not the speed.
The resultant force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, $F = ma$, and the acceleration is in the same direction as the resultant force.
